audit_findings.title: The anchor mixes fundamentally different pre- and post-Marcum businesses
audit_findings.magnitude: $914.2 million of acquired-operation revenue, representing 50.4% of 2025 incremental revenue; $75.6 million gap between $250.3 million latest OE and $174.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The structural break affects normalized OE and makes the legacy-heavy log trend an unreliable anchor for the post-Marcum earnings claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Revenue from newly acquired operations, net of divestitures, contributed $914.2 million, or 50.4%, of incremental revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the same period in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The change in business scale is demonstrated, while the direction of anchor error is unresolved. Because half of incremental 2025 revenue came from acquisitions and the chosen anchor is 30.2% below latest OE, a coherent post-Transaction baseline could reasonably change every scenario and the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using full-year post-Marcum pro forma OE with current interest expense, complete share consideration and separately identified integration effects; compare that anchor with $174.7 million.

audit_findings.title: Recurring acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $160.7 million cash payments across 2023-2025 ($45.2 million, $56.8 million and $58.7 million), averaging $53.6 million annually; $21.012 million liability at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash acquisition consideration omitted from operating OE or the equity bridge leaves less cash for common owners; stock settlements may also increase the share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: 2025 - Net cash provided by financing activities in 2025 consisted of $51.5 million net proceeds from our 2024 Credit Facilities and a net increase of $30.8 million in client fund obligations, partially offset by $160.1 million used to repurchase shares, $7.8 million used to repurchase shares for tax withholding purposes, $58.7 million of contingent consideration payments for prior acquisitions, $1.0 million deferred financing fees paid in connection with the 2024 Credit Facilities, and $0.5 million used for payments of notes payable.
audit_findings.explanation: The payments and the omission from operating cash flow are demonstrated, but their sustainable economic portion is unresolved. The three-year average equals 30.7% of the $174.7 million anchor, so treating recurring acquisition consideration as costless growth could materially overstate value. The current recorded liability alone is only about $0.34 per diluted share, but it does not capture the demonstrated recurring-payment issue.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $21.012 million current and noncurrent liability, probable cash and stock settlements, and historical acquisition payments; rerun OE and shares for any portion required to maintain the earnings base.

audit_findings.title: Large Marcum integration costs may improperly depress sustainable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $64.3 million of 2025 operating integration costs, plus $24.8 million of 2025 Transaction-related G&A costs; $46.3 million of integration costs in the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary costs retained in reported earnings reduce the 2025 OE observation and the fitted OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025, included approximately $64.3 million costs related to the Transaction for integration, and operating expenses for the year ended December 31, 2024, included approximately $5.0 million in costs related to the Transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The costs are demonstrated, but their inclusion in the OE calculation and their temporary versus recurring character are unresolved. The disclosed 2025 amounts total $89.1 million, equal to 51.0% of the $174.7 million anchor, and continued 2026 spending shows that simply removing all costs would also be unsafe. A properly supported normalization could materially raise value.
audit_findings.action: Trace each Transaction and integration cost into OE, classify finite versus recurring systems, occupancy, restructuring and acquisition-program spending, then rerun the anchor using only supported adjustments.

audit_findings.title: The D&A add-back may ignore economic depletion of acquired client relationships
audit_findings.magnitude: $74.9 million of 2025 intangible amortization, equal to 42.9% of the $174.7 million anchor; $73.2 million estimated for 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquired-intangible amortization without an offsetting maintenance charge can overstate OE and all resulting operating values.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense for client lists and other intangible assets was $ 74.9 million, $ 32.7 million and $ 23.8 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: No economic-depletion error is yet demonstrated because client-retention costs may already be expensed through compensation and marketing. Nevertheless, amortization is large and persistent relative to anchor OE, so even a partial evidence-based maintenance charge could materially reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Measure client-list attrition, retention spending and replacement-acquisition requirements; rerun OE with an evidence-based maintenance charge while avoiding double counting expenses already recorded.

audit_findings.title: ASA/VIE structure creates an unreserved contingent claim on CBIZ
audit_findings.mechanism: Support of an insolvent CPA firm or uncovered attest liability would create a cash claim ahead of common equity, reducing future OE or requiring a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event that the CPA firms with which we maintain ASAs incur judgments and costs related to such suits that threaten the solvency of the CPA firms, we could incur expenditures related to such proceedings, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a disclosed forward-looking contingency, not a demonstrated present liability. The filings say the VIE accounts are not material, CBIZ does not expect to bear attest losses, and no presently material indemnification obligation is identified; however, $651.2 million of 2025 ASA revenue shows meaningful economic exposure if support becomes necessary.
audit_findings.action: Monitor CPA-firm capitalization, insurance limits, indemnities, litigation and regulatory claims; open and quantify a bridge or OE adjustment if probable support obligations or uninsured exposures emerge.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring legal-settlement gain may remain in 2025 owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.5 million pre-tax, equal to 7.2% of the $174.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the one-time gain increases 2025 OE and marginally raises the legacy-plus-2025 log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of the settlement of that litigation, the Company received a settlement payment of $ 12.5 million, which was recorded as a pre-tax gain in "Other income, net" on the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in OE is unresolved, but the filed gain is small relative to the anchor and correcting it can only reduce value. The current price of $54.85 already exceeds the $46.89 bull value by $7.96, or 17.0% of bull value, so removing this gain cannot reverse the valuation conclusion and would instead reinforce it.
audit_findings.action: Trace the gain through the 2025 OE calculation and remove its after-tax contribution if included; no broader valuation redesign is required for this item.
